original_question: In foundational particle physics, determine whether there is a physically meaningful aether-like fluid; whether the new electron theory proposed by Dirac in 1951 can resolve the infinity problem in quantum electrodynamics and reconcile the quantum-mechanical and electrodynamical descriptions of the electron; whether the mixing matrix appearing in a lepton-mass formula has an underlying dynamical mechanism; whether neutrinos have mass; whether composite models of elementary particles built from more fundamental constituents called rishons or preons predict phenomena better than standard quantum chromodynamics; whether quark confinement has a physical explanation; and whether quantum chromodynamics has a theoretical link to quantum fluid dynamics.
target_in_paper: Section 1.1 (Problems in elementary particles etc.), specifically the itemized open-problem list in items (i)–(viii) on particle-physics foundations, from the Dirac-ether question through the possible QCD/quantum-fluid connection. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already tracks the paper very closely: it captures all eight themes and almost the same ordering as the Section 1.1 list—Dirac ether, two questions about Dirac's 1951 electron theory, Koide's lepton-mass matrix, neutrino mass, rishon/preon models versus conventional QCD, quark confinement, and a possible QCD–quantum-fluid link. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
missing_details: The first item is tied specifically to Dirac's ether proposal, not to a generic ether-like medium. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The paper states two separate Dirac-1951 questions: one asks about solving the infinity problem, and the next asks about reconciling quantum-mechanical and electrodynamical pictures of the electron. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The lepton-mass question is not about an unspecified matrix: it is explicitly about the Koide mixing matrix and asks for its dynamical basis. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The rishon/preon question is explicitly comparative, asking whether that model predicts better than conventional QCD. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

The paper frames the whole cluster as open questions in theoretical/particle physics, immediately after a discussion of unresolved issues in QED and QCD and renewed interest in Dirac's 1951 theory; that scope should be retained. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))

No formal mathematical notation, variables, operators, ambient fields/rings, degree conditions, nilpotency assumptions, or asymptotic quantifiers are given for this problem cluster; the formulation is conceptual rather than theorem-style. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
refined_question: In the scope of Section 1.1, can one determine whether a Dirac-type ether exists; whether Dirac's 1951 theory can remove the QED infinity difficulty; whether that theory reconciles the quantum-mechanical and electrodynamical descriptions of the electron; what dynamical mechanism underlies Koide's lepton-mass mixing matrix; whether neutrinos are massive; whether rishon/preon models of elementary particles predict better than conventional QCD; what physical mechanism explains quark confinement; and whether QCD is theoretically connected to quantum fluid dynamics? ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
justification: The draft is not aiming at a theorem, conjecture, or proposition elsewhere in the paper; this 2006 work is a survey/book of open problems, and the nearest official formulation is exactly the eight-item list in Section 1.1 after the discussion of QED, QCD, and Dirac's dissatisfaction with standard QED. Because the paper gives no formal notation or proved equivalence here, the most faithful refinement is to preserve the eight linked questions, restore the named objects used in the paper, and avoid broadening the target beyond Section 1.1. ([cds.cern.ch](https://cds.cern.ch/record/2847617/files/arXiv%3Amath_0609238.pdf))
